validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2021 does not match either independent source I could find. CARE Ratings' two press releases (13-Sep-2023 and 08-Dec-2025, both confirmed via pdftotext, verifier false-negative documented above) state unambiguously: 'GITL commissioned phase-I of the MBBVPL on October 14, 2019.' The wiki's own cited source (PNGRB's 'Partially Commissioned Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines', 31 March 2021 edition) only documents that the pipeline WAS ALREADY commissioned as of that March-2021 snapshot -- it is a status-as-of date, not a commissioning date, and 2021 is also exactly when CARE separately notes 'RFCL commissioned its urea project in March 2021' (a different asset -- the customer's fertiliser plant, not GITL's pipeline). The most likely explanation is that GEM's StartYear1 was set from the March-2021 PNGRB snapshot (or from RFCL's own March-2021 COD) rather than from GITL's actual commissioning date, which is a full 17 months earlier. I could not find a second, organizationally distinct source giving the specific Oct-2019 date (CARE's two reports share one analyst house, so I'm treating them as one origin for tier purposes), so tier=medium rather than high, though I'm confident in the direction of the correction given CARE repeats the identical date across two independently-commissioned annual credit reviews three years apart, each presumably re-verified against GITL's own filings.

validity.recommendation: flag/verify Capacity=78.25 MMSCMD for this 'Phase I' row -- independent sourcing indicates the ACTUAL design capacity of the 365 km built/operating Phase I stretch is only ~4.5-5 MMSCMD (of which ~2.02 MMSCMD is contracted to RFCL); 78.25 (rounds to PNGRB's 78.3) is the AUTHORISED/system-wide design capacity for the FULL 1,881 km project once entirely built (Phase I + the still-under-construction 1,517 km Phase II), not the capacity of the segment this row actually describes
validity.researcher_notes: This is the most material finding on the row. GEM's Capacity=78.25 MMSCMD for the 'Phase I' segment matches PNGRB's regulator table almost exactly (78.3 MMSCMD, 1dp rounding) -- but that PNGRB figure is explicitly the 'Authorised/Design Capacity' for the ENTIRE GITL entity/project (Authorised Length column = 1,881 km, i.e. the whole corridor, not the 365 km operating stretch). Two independently-sourced, organizationally distinct citations establish the actual built Phase-I capacity is far smaller: (a) CARE Ratings, in both its 2023 and 2025 press releases (same house, but each an independently re-verified annual credit review): 'The design capacity of phase-I is ~4.50 mmscmd [2025]/around 5 mmscmd [2023], of which ~2.02 mmscmd is supplied to RFCL under a GTA'. (b) Business Standard, a mainstream Indian business daily, reporting contemporaneously in July 2016 on the signing of the actual RFCL Gas Transportation Agreement (https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/gitl-signs-transportation-agreement-with-ramagundam-fertilizers-for-20-years-116071500658_1.html, verified OK): 'Under the agreement, GITL will supply 2 mmscmd of natural gas from Mallavaram of Andhra Pradesh to RFCL's plant at Ramagundam' -- an independent, decade-old, pre-CARE confirmation that the actual contracted/designed throughput for this exact stretch is single-digit MMSCMD, not 78. The mechanism is also independently explained: CARE's disclosures (and a related PNGRB/GITL diameter dispute, corroborated in a November-2019 APTEL appellate tribunal judgment I located via indiankanoon.org/aptel.gov.in but could NOT cite -- both mirrors failed url_verifier, one on a gov.in SSL certificate-chain error and one on a 403, so I am not proposing them as refs, only reporting what I read) state GITL built the 364.42 km Phase-I stretch at 18-inch diameter instead of the originally-contracted 42-inch, specifically 'leading to reduced capacity with respect to the authorised capacity' -- i.e. the smaller pipe physically cannot carry anywhere near the 78 MMSCMD full-system design figure. I am NOT proposing a replacement Capacity value myself (per the no-forced-numbers guidance and because 4.5 vs ~5 vs the CARE 2.02-contracted figure are three different granularities of the same underlying fact) -- this is a genuine value disagreement for Update to resolve, most likely by changing Capacity to ~4.5-5 MMSCMD for this Phase-I-scoped row (or by adding a ResearcherNotes caveat if GEM deliberately intends this field to describe the ultimate system capacity rather than this segment's actual capacity). tier=high: CARE and Business Standard are two organizationally independent origins, seven years apart, agreeing on the same order-of-magnitude, non-78 figure.

validity.researcher_notes: The Owner tab lists Owner1='Gujarat State Petronet' at 100%. Two problems, both independently sourced: (1) 'Gujarat State Petronet Limited' (GSPL) and 'GSPL India Transco Limited' (GITL) are two distinct, separately rated legal entities -- GSPL is a listed gas-transmission company (CARE AA+), and GITL is a special-purpose JV vehicle it co-founded specifically to build MBBVPL. Gem.wiki's own infobox (read for leads, not cited) lists Owner/Operator/Parent company as 'GSPL India Transco Limited (GITL)', not 'Gujarat State Petronet' directly. (2) Even treating GSPL as the intended ultimate parent, CARE Ratings' 2023 and 2025 press releases state the actual JV shareholding is 'GSPL (52%), IOCL (26%), BPCL (11%) and HPCL (11%)' -- GSPL holds a majority, not 100%. Business Standard's independent 2016 article (https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/gitl-signs-transportation-agreement-with-ramagundam-fertilizers-for-20-years-116071500658_1.html, verified OK) corroborates the corporate-family relationship from a wholly separate, decade-earlier origin: 'GSPL India Transco Ltd (GITL), a subsidiary of Gujarat State Petronet Ltd (GSPL)' -- consistent with a majority (52%) stake, and inconsistent with a simple 100%-owned entity being renamed/conflated with its parent. tier=high: CARE (for the precise percentages) and Business Standard (for the distinct-entity/subsidiary relationship, independently and earlier) are organizationally separate origins agreeing GITL is not simply '100% Gujarat State Petronet'.
